column1: # Findings in what sheaf writes that its Arlington tests allow, each held for a backlog entry, in pdf-lint's allowances format
# (sheaf-pdf/pdf-lint): the table and key of the row the finding breaks, its rule, the corpus file it's in (* for any), the PDF
# version of the files it's allowed in, and later ones' (* for any), and why, the entry first (B40: …). A row any file may use
# must be needed by a default test (every_allowance_for_any_file_is_needed), a row for one corpus file by the corpus tier
# (just tier-arlington), and every reason must start with an open backlog entry (every_allowance_names_an_open_backlog_entry).

column6: B40: The model has no CA in AnnotSquare before PDF 2.0 (tsv/latest says since 2.0; its tsv/1.7 has none), though ISO 32000-1 Table 170 gives every markup annotation /CA from 1.4 and Table 169 makes Square one; AnnotCircle, Square's twin in Table 177, has it from 1.4. A model error, to report upstream.

B41: A connector is a Link annotation, written with the keys every mark has: /CA, which a Link has only from PDF 2.0 (ISO 32000-2 Table 166), and /T and /CreationDate, which no Link has. sheaf reads its opacity back from /CA; writing it elsewhere, or raising the file to 2.0, is a design question.

B42: sheaf's marks never raise the file's PDF version: what they write came in 1.4 (/NM, /CA, their appearances' transparency) to 1.7 (an attachment's /UF, a measurement's /Measure), and a mark on an older file leaves its version as it was. Raising it writes the catalog, a change no signature allows (M10.5 9.3). Ruled (Greg, 2026-10-24): marks raise the version when the save has no signatures to keep, in this entry's own PR; until then this row holds the finding, and after it, a mark on a signed file.

B43: sheaf writes the standard 14 fonts it draws with (a header, a watermark, a mark's appearance) as /BaseFont alone, without /FirstChar, /LastChar, /Widths and /FontDescriptor, which PDF 2.0 asks of every simple font (ISO 32000-2 Table 109; optional for the standard 14 only before 2.0), so this row holds 2.0 files only: before 2.0, a font sheaf builds without them that isn't one of the standard 14 still fails. Writing them, always or in 2.0 files only, changes every font resource sheaf writes.

This encrypted form's pages have an InDesign /PieceInfo, whose /DocumentID is one, and no /LastModified: a save that moves a page into an object stream, or out of one, shows the finding otherwise than the form, and it isn't carried.

F29: The form's startxref names byte 84932, where there's no cross-reference (qpdf says so, and its reconstruction fails too). pdf-lint's bytes reader reads what's written and reaches none of the fields that sheaf, reading through lopdf's recovery, merges into both Rewrites, so their /DR, deprecated from PDF 1.5, isn't carried (78 findings).

F29: The form's startxref names byte 600541, where there's no object (qpdf says so, and reconstructs the cross-references). pdf-lint's bytes reader reads what's written and reaches nothing from the trailer, where sheaf, reading through lopdf's recovery, merges the pages into both Rewrites, so their /Tabs, too new for the form's PDF 1.4, isn't carried (9 findings).
